---
name: project-git
description: How git works in an Archon Horizon workspace — one out-of-tree workspace ledger (no per-project repos); read a project's history by pathspec or by a session's commit trailers.
---

Read this before running `git diff`/`git log` on a project.

## The model

- **One out-of-tree workspace ledger.** Archon commits to a single repo whose git
  dir is `.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git` with the workspace **root** as its
  work tree (driven via `--git-dir`/`--work-tree`). `<root>/.git` is deliberately
  untouched — it is reserved for a user repo. The ledger records one commit per
  completed session: `config.yaml`, the session's scoped project files, and
  `.archon-horizon/` shared state; never the binary git dirs under
  `.archon-horizon/vcs/`, locks, or other volatile internals.
- **There are no per-project repositories.** A project directory has no nested
  `.git/`, and there is no `.archon-horizon/vcs/<project>.git`. A project's
  "history" is simply the workspace ledger filtered to that project's path.
- **You record your own work by committing to the ledger** with plain `git` (see
  below). Commit *early and often* with a semantic, math-first message — the
  commit message + diff is how your progress is read, so make the message say what
  you proved/built. Provenance trailers are added automatically; do not write them.

So a plain `git diff` at the root sees only a user repo (if any), never Archon's.
Drive the out-of-tree workspace ledger explicitly (or use `hgit`).

## Recording your work (committing)

Commits go to the ledger, **not** to `<root>/.git` and **not** via any project
`.git` (there is none). Do **not** `export GIT_DIR` / `GIT_WORK_TREE` yourself — that
would redirect `lake` and other tooling. Two equivalent ways to commit:

```bash
# 1) The `hgit` wrapper (on the session env as $HORIZON_GIT) — plain git, ledger-scoped:
"$HORIZON_GIT" add path/to/File.lean
"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "feat(chapter): prove foo_lemma" \
  --trailer 'Summary=**Proof.** Closed the compactness step using $K \subseteq X$.'

# 2) The explicit form (identical effect):
git --git-dir="$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree="$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" \
    add path/to/File.lean
git --git-dir="$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree="$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" \
    commit -m "feat(chapter): prove foo_lemma" \
    --trailer 'Summary=**Proof.** Closed the compactness step using $K \subseteq X$.'
```

Ordinary git: the ledger's index tracks HEAD, so `add` then `commit` records your
files on top of it. Horizon's own commits stage in a private index and never leave
anything staged in your way.

- **Prefer the pathspec commit** — name the paths on the commit itself:
  `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "…" --trailer 'Summary=…' -- path/to/File.lean`
  It records exactly those files, ignores whatever else may be staged, and git
  builds its tree from the **current** HEAD — so it cannot silently revert a
  concurrent session's files the way a commit built on a stale index can.
- Add at least one **`Summary` trailer** explaining the important change, not
  merely repeating the subject. Use one trailer per distinct explanation when
  useful. Its value supports Markdown and LaTeX, so concise mathematical context
  such as `--trailer 'Summary=**Invariant.** Preserves $f(x)=x$ on $A$.'` renders

9	/-!
10	# The widened cover datum: arbitrary affine opens (R2, human decision I-0492)
11	
12	`FinCoverData` (`Picard/DivisorFamily.lean`) types its pieces INTO a fixed pair of pinned
13	`P¹` charts — `h₀ : Fin m₀ → Γ(V₀)`, `h₁ : Fin m₁ → Γ(V₁)`, `pieces = Sum.elim (basicOpen ∘
14	h₀) (basicOpen ∘ h₁)` — with a partition of unity on EACH chart.  Per-piece swallow-or-miss
15	needs only openness (`DivSchemeCertZarConn.lean`), and it is the chart-wise partitions that
16	upgrade "inside one piece" to "inside one chart"; that upgrade is the obstruction, and no
17	repair keeping the pieces inside the preimages of a fixed pair of points of `P¹` can work
18	(`informal/spec-dd-r.md` ADDENDUM 3 §2, ADDENDUM 4 §4.4).
19	
20	This file carries the widened datum.  A piece is an **arbitrary affine open** of the
21	relative curve, the index is a bare `Fin m`, and the covering condition is **joint**
22	(`⨆ j, pieces j = ⊤`) rather than chart-wise.  Nothing types a piece into a chart.
23	
24	Justification for the shape, used and not re-derived (I-0492 clause 2): `supp D` is finite
25	over `R`, hence lies in a single affine open of `C ×_k Spec R` (Stacks `0B8B`), so a cover
26	with one straddling piece always exists.
27	
28	## What the widening RELOCATES rather than removes (I-0492 clause 4(ii))
29	
30	The old typing was silently supplying two things that now have to be earned:
31	
32	* **every point lies in a piece** — was `relCover_sup` plus the two partitions; now it is
33	  exactly the joint covering field (`AffCoverData.exists_mem_pieces`);
34	* **`Γ(pieces j)` is `R`-flat** — was `flat_sections_basicOpen` over
35	  `flat_sections_relPinnedChart`, i.e. it rested on `Γ(V_bᴿ) ≅ R ⊗[k] Γ(C, V_b)` being FREE.
36	  For an arbitrary affine open that route is gone.  Replacement, and it is the one genuinely
37	  new commutative-algebra input the widening costs: `relCurve C R ↘ Spec R` is flat (it is
38	  the base change of `C.hom` along `overSpec k R`, and a morphism to a field spectrum is
39	  flat), and a flat morphism has `R`-flat sections on every affine open
40	  (`flat_sections_of_flat_hom`).  Unconditional in `R` — no Noetherian, no finiteness.
41	
42	Fibrewise-finite support (I-0492 clause 4(i)) is deliberately NOT here: it is not a property
43	of a cover, it must come from the seed's own degree data, and it may not hide inside a
44	`LocalEquations` or an adaptation field.
45	
46	## Main declarations
47	
48	* `AlgebraicGeometry.flat_sections_of_flat_hom` — sections of an arbitrary affine open of a
49	  scheme flat over the base ring are flat.
50	* `AlgebraicGeometry.instFlatRelCurveHom` — the relative curve is flat over its test base.
51	* `AlgebraicGeometry.AffCoverData` — the widened cover datum.
52	* `AffCoverData.exists_mem_pieces`, `isAffineOpen_pieces`, `flat_sections_pieces`,
53	  `flat_sections_pieces_inf` — the derived replacements for what the chart typing supplied.
54	* `AlgebraicGeometry.FinCoverData.toAffCoverData` — the migration: old data instantiates the
55	  widened datum, so nothing landed becomes unreachable.
56	-/

71	
72	The engine that replaces the pinned-chart freeness argument. -/

74	section FlatSections
75	
76	variable (K : Type u) [CommRing K] (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (.of K))]
77	
78	/-- **Sections of an arbitrary affine open are flat, for a scheme flat over the base ring.**
79	`Scheme.overAlgebraMap` factors as `ΓSpecIso.inv` followed by the structure morphism's
80	`appLE ⊤ V`; the second is `RingHom.Flat` because `AlgebraicGeometry.Flat` is a
81	`HasRingHomProperty` for `RingHom.Flat` and `V` is affine, the first is flat because it is a
82	ring isomorphism, and `RingHom.Flat` composes.
83	
84	This is the widened replacement for `flat_sections_basicOpen ∘ flat_sections_relPinnedChart`:
85	that pair needed the open to be a basic open of a chart whose sections are a FREE base
86	change, which is exactly what an arbitrary affine open does not give. -/
87	theorem flat_sections_of_flat_hom [AlgebraicGeometry.Flat (X ↘ Spec (.of K))]
88	    {V : X.Opens} (hV : IsAffineOpen V) :
89	    Module.Flat K Γ(X, V) := by
90	  have happ : RingHom.Flat ((X ↘ Spec (.of K)).appLE ⊤ V (by simp)).hom :=
91	    HasRingHomProperty.appLE (P := @AlgebraicGeometry.Flat)
92	      (f := X ↘ Spec (.of K)) inferInstance ⟨⊤, isAffineOpen_top _⟩ ⟨V, hV⟩ (by simp)
93	  have hiso : RingHom.Flat ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of K)).inv).hom :=
94	    RingHom.Flat.of_bijective
95	      (ConcreteCategory.bijective_of_isIso (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of K)).inv)
96	  have hcomp : RingHom.Flat (X.overAlgebraMap K V) := by
97	    have hfac : X.overAlgebraMap K V
98	        = ((X ↘ Spec (.of K)).appLE ⊤ V (by simp)).hom.comp
99	            ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of K)).inv).hom := by
100	      rw [Scheme.overAlgebraMap, Scheme.Hom.appLE]
101	      rfl
102	    rw [hfac]
103	    exact RingHom.Flat.comp hiso happ
104	  exact (RingHom.flat_algebraMap_iff (R := K) (S := Γ(X, V))).mp hcomp
105	
106	end FlatSections

110	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
111	variable (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
112	
113	/-- **The relative curve is flat over its test base.** `(snd C (overSpec k R)).left` is the
114	base change of `C.hom` along `(overSpec k R).hom` (`Over.isPullback_left`), and every
115	structure morphism to the spectrum of a field is flat (`flat_hom_over_field`). -/
116	instance instFlatRelCurveHom : AlgebraicGeometry.Flat (relCurve C R ↘ Spec (.of R)) :=
117	  AlgebraicGeometry.Flat.isStableUnderBaseChange.of_isPullback
118	    (Over.isPullback_left C (overSpec k R)) inferInstance
119	
120	/-- **Flat sections on an arbitrary affine open of the relative curve** — the widened
121	(c1)-flatness input, with no chart and no freeness. -/
122	theorem flat_sections_isAffineOpen {V : (relCurve C R).Opens} (hV : IsAffineOpen V) :
123	    Module.Flat R Γ(relCurve C R, V) :=
124	  flat_sections_of_flat_hom R (relCurve C R) hV

128	/-! ## The widened cover datum -/
129	
130	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
131	variable (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
132	variable (π : C.left ⟶ P1 k)
133	
134	/-- **The widened cover datum** (R2, human decision I-0492): finitely many **arbitrary
135	affine opens** of the relative curve that **jointly** cover it.
136	
137	Contrast with `FinCoverData`, which this replaces on the certificate side: there is no `h₀`,
138	no `h₁`, no `a₀`/`a₁`, no `partition₀`/`partition₁`, no `Sum` index, and above all no typing
139	of a piece into a pinned chart.  The chart-wise partitions of unity are exactly what upgraded
140	per-piece swallow-or-miss to a chart statement, and they are gone deliberately; the two-chart
141	structure the Θ-layer needs is carried separately (see `ChartTyping` below), never by the
142	certificate clauses.
143	
144	`Type u`, like `FinCoverData`, so a functor value can quotient it. -/
145	structure AffCoverData : Type u where
146	  /-- The number of pieces. -/
147	  m : ℕ
148	  /-- The pieces: arbitrary opens of the relative curve, made affine by `isAffineOpen`. -/
149	  pieces : Fin m → (relCurve C R).Opens
150	  /-- Every piece is affine — the only geometric demand the certificate layer makes. -/
151	  isAffineOpen : ∀ j, IsAffineOpen (pieces j)
152	  /-- The pieces cover the curve JOINTLY.  This replaces the two chart-wise partitions of
153	  unity, and it is the whole structural content of the widening. -/
154	  cover : (⨆ j, pieces j) = ⊤
155	
156	namespace AffCoverData
157	
158	variable {C R π} (D : AffCoverData C R)
159	
160	/-- The gluing index of the widened datum: a bare `Fin`, with no two-sided structure. -/
161	abbrev index : Type := Fin D.m
162	
163	/-- **Every point lies in a piece.** Under `FinCoverData` this came from `relCover_sup`
164	together with the two partitions of unity; here it is exactly the joint covering field —
165	obligation I-0492 4(ii) discharged in one line rather than silently supplied by the typing. -/
166	lemma exists_mem_pieces (z : relCurve C R) : ∃ j : D.index, z ∈ D.pieces j := by
167	  have hz : z ∈ (⨆ j, D.pieces j) := by rw [D.cover]; trivial
168	  exact Opens.mem_iSup.mp hz
169	
170	/-- The pieces are affine opens — by fiat now, rather than as basic opens of an affine
171	chart. -/
172	lemma isAffineOpen_pieces (j : D.index) : IsAffineOpen (D.pieces j) :=
173	  D.isAffineOpen j
174	
175	/-- **Flatness of the piece section rings over the test ring.** The widened replacement for
176	`FinCoverData.flat_sections_pieces`, which localized a FREE pinned-chart ring; here it is the
177	flat structure morphism of the relative curve read on an affine open. -/
178	theorem flat_sections_pieces (j : D.index) :
179	    Module.Flat R Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j) :=
180	  flat_sections_isAffineOpen C R (D.isAffineOpen j)
181	
182	/-- Piece overlaps are affine (the relative curve is separated over `Spec R`, being proper),
183	so the overlap section rings are flat too — the widened
184	`FinCoverData.flat_sections_pieces_inf`. -/
185	theorem flat_sections_pieces_inf (i j : D.index)
186	    (hinf : IsAffineOpen (D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j)) :
187	    Module.Flat R Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j) :=
188	  flat_sections_isAffineOpen C R hinf
189	
190	end AffCoverData
191	
192	/-! ## The optional chart typing, for the Θ-layer only -/
193	
194	/-- The pinned chart of a given side, spelled here so this file needs no import from the
195	Θ-layer (it agrees with `relPinnedChart` by `rfl`). -/
196	noncomputable def pinnedChartOfSide [IsAffineHom π] (b : Bool) : (relCurve C R).Opens :=
197	  bif b then (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ else (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀
198	
199	/-- **A chart typing of a widened cover**: an assignment of each piece to one of the two
200	pinned `P¹` charts, containing it.  This is what the Θ-twisting unit genuinely needs (the
201	theta cocycle lives on `V₀ ⊓ V₁`), and it is deliberately a SEPARATE datum: no certificate
202	clause and no locally-certified predicate may require it.  Keeping it separate is what stops
203	the old fixed-pair typing from being smuggled back in through a field. -/
204	structure ChartTyping [IsAffineHom π] (D : AffCoverData C R) where
205	  /-- Which pinned chart the piece is assigned to. -/
206	  side : D.index → Bool
207	  /-- The piece is contained in its assigned chart. -/
208	  piece_le : ∀ j, D.pieces j ≤ pinnedChartOfSide C R π (side j)
209	
210	/-! ## Migration: old cover data instantiates the widened datum -/
211	
212	namespace FinCoverData
213	
214	variable {C R π} [IsAffineHom π] (D : FinCoverData C R π)
215	
216	/-- **The migration map.** An old chart-typed `FinCoverData` gives a widened
217	`AffCoverData`: reindex `Fin m₀ ⊕ Fin m₁` through `finSumFinEquiv`, the pieces are affine as
218	basic opens of the affine pinned charts, and the joint cover follows from the two chart-wise
219	covers together with `relCover_sup`.
220	
221	The point of this lemma is that widening costs nothing landed: every existing construction of
222	cover data still produces a legal widened datum.  The converse fails, and that is exactly the
223	content of R2. -/
224	noncomputable def toAffCoverData : AffCoverData C R where
225	  m := D.m₀ + D.m₁
226	  pieces := fun j => D.pieces (finSumFinEquiv.symm j)
227	  isAffineOpen := fun j => by
228	    rcases finSumFinEquiv.symm j with i | i
229	    · rw [FinCoverData.pieces_inl]
230	      exact (relCover_isAffineOpen₀ C R (fiberTwoCover π)).basicOpen _
231	    · rw [FinCoverData.pieces_inr]
232	      exact (relCover_isAffineOpen₁ C R (fiberTwoCover π)).basicOpen _
233	  cover := by
234	    refine top_le_iff.mp fun z _ => ?_
235	    -- every point is in a pinned chart, and each chart is covered by its own pieces
236	    have hz : z ∈ (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀
237	        ⊔ (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ := by
238	      rw [relCover_sup]; trivial
239	    have key : ∃ i : D.index, z ∈ D.pieces i := by
240	      rcases Opens.mem_sup.mp hz with h | h
241	      · obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ := Opens.mem_iSup.mp (D.cover₀ h)
242	        exact ⟨Sum.inl i, hi⟩
243	      · obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ := Opens.mem_iSup.mp (D.cover₁ h)
244	        exact ⟨Sum.inr i, hi⟩
245	    obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ := key
246	    exact Opens.mem_iSup.mpr ⟨finSumFinEquiv i, by
247	      simpa only [Equiv.symm_apply_apply] using hi⟩
248	
249	@[simp]
250	lemma toAffCoverData_pieces (j : Fin (D.m₀ + D.m₁)) :
251	    D.toAffCoverData.pieces j = D.pieces (finSumFinEquiv.symm j) := rfl
252	
253	/-- The canonical chart typing of a migrated datum: chart-0 pieces are basic opens of `V₀`,
254	chart-1 pieces of `V₁`. -/
255	noncomputable def toChartTyping : ChartTyping C R π D.toAffCoverData where
256	  side := fun j => (finSumFinEquiv.symm j).isRight
257	  piece_le := fun j => by
258	    rw [toAffCoverData_pieces]
259	    rcases h : finSumFinEquiv.symm j with i | i
260	    · rw [FinCoverData.pieces_inl]
261	      exact (relCurve C R).basicOpen_le (D.h₀ i)
262	    · rw [FinCoverData.pieces_inr]
263	      exact (relCurve C R).basicOpen_le (D.h₁ i)
264	
265	end FinCoverData

8	/-!
9	# Reindexing a widened cover and its certificate along an index equivalence
10	
11	The transport `DivisorFamilyAffZar.lean` flagged as this lane's remaining obligation.  Clauses
12	(c1) of `AffAdaptation.IsCertified` are pointwise and transport by relabelling, but
13	(c2)/(c3)/(c4) concern `gluedSubmodule`, a kernel inside `∀ j : index, colength j`, so they
14	need the equalizer carried along the index equivalence.
15	
16	The trick that makes this painless is to reindex the COVER so that its pieces are *definitionally*
17	`D.pieces (e j)`.  Then the adaptation's equations need no transport at all — the section rings
18	are literally the same — and the certificate transport is `LinearEquiv.piCongrLeft` on the
19	index, which intertwines `deltaLeft`/`deltaRight` because reindexing acts diagonally on the
20	pair index as well.  `Module.rankAtStalk` is invariant along a linear equivalence
21	(`Module.rankAtStalk_eq_of_equiv`).
22	
23	This is the general form of what the chart-typed → widened comparison needs: `toAffCoverData`
24	already defines its pieces as `D.pieces (finSumFinEquiv.symm j)`, i.e. exactly this shape.
25	
26	## Main declarations
27	
28	* `AlgebraicGeometry.AffCoverData.reindex` — the cover relabelled along `e : ι ≃ D.index`
29	  (pieces definitionally `D.pieces (e j)`).
30	* `AffAdaptation.reindex` — the adaptation on it, with equations transported by `rfl`.
31	* `AffAdaptation.colength_reindex` — the colength modules are literally the same.
32	* `AffAdaptation.chartProdCongr` — the product identification, `piCongrLeft` on the index.
33	-/

52	/-- **The cover relabelled along an index equivalence.**  The pieces are *definitionally*
53	`D.pieces (e j)`, which is what makes the certificate transport below free of coercions. -/
54	noncomputable def reindex (D : AffCoverData C R) {m' : ℕ} (e : Fin m' ≃ D.index) :
55	    AffCoverData C R where
56	  m := m'
57	  pieces := fun j => D.pieces (e j)
58	  isAffineOpen := fun j => D.isAffineOpen (e j)

60	    refine top_le_iff.mp fun z _ => ?_
61	    obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ := D.exists_mem_pieces z
62	    exact Opens.mem_iSup.mpr ⟨e.symm i, by simpa only [Equiv.apply_symm_apply] using hi⟩

113	/-! ## The glued clauses transport
114	
115	The overlap structure of a relabelled adaptation is DEFINITIONALLY the original one relabelled
116	(`ovlColength_reindex`, `toOvlLeft_reindex` — both `rfl`), which is what makes the equalizer
117	transport a one-liner rather than the hundred lines the earlier estimate assumed. -/
118	
119	/-- The overlap colengths of a relabelled adaptation are the original ones, relabelled. -/
120	lemma ovlColength_reindex (A : AffAdaptation D d) {m' : ℕ} (e : Fin m' ≃ D.index)
121	    (i j : Fin m') :
122	    (A.reindex e).ovlColength i j = A.ovlColength (e i) (e j) := rfl
123	
124	/-- The left overlap arrow of a relabelled adaptation is the original one, relabelled. -/
125	lemma toOvlLeft_reindex (A : AffAdaptation D d) {m' : ℕ} (e : Fin m' ≃ D.index)
126	    (i j : Fin m') :
127	    (A.reindex e).toOvlLeft i j = A.toOvlLeft (e i) (e j) := rfl
128	
129	/-- The right overlap arrow of a relabelled adaptation is the original one, relabelled. -/
130	lemma toOvlRight_reindex (A : AffAdaptation D d) {m' : ℕ} (e : Fin m' ≃ D.index)
131	    (i j : Fin m') :
132	    (A.reindex e).toOvlRight i j = A.toOvlRight (e i) (e j) := rfl
133	
134	/-- **The glued submodule transports.**  A section of the relabelled product lies in its
135	glued submodule exactly when the corresponding overlap identities hold for the ORIGINAL
136	arrows, read at the relabelled indices.  Both sides unfold to the same family of identities
137	because every overlap datum of `A.reindex e` is `rfl`-equal to that of `A` at `(e i, e j)`;
138	the pair index is quantified in the relabelled coordinates, which keeps the statement
139	dependently well-typed. -/
140	lemma mem_gluedSubmodule_reindex_iff (A : AffAdaptation D d) {m' : ℕ} (e : Fin m' ≃ D.index)
141	    (s : (A.reindex e).chartProd) :

10	
11	Roadmap leaf `AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-d.ddr.certificate.swallow-adapt`, restated over
12	`AffCoverData`.  The chart-pair version (`DivSchemeCertZarChartPair.lean`) is landed but
13	consumes chart principality, which is false for an arbitrary degree-`n` divisor on a curve of
14	genus `≥ 1` (`informal/spec-dd-r.md` ADDENDUM 3 corrigendum C4(i)): `Cl(V_b) ≠ 0` and
15	shrinking `Spec R` does not change a fibre class.  Over a widened cover the shape is
16	different and the obstruction does not arise: **one piece swallows the support and every
17	other piece misses it.**
18	
19	## The geometric input, supplied as a HYPOTHESIS and not re-derived
20	
21	The decision (I-0492 clause 2) says to USE, not re-derive: `supp D` is finite over `R`, hence
22	lies in a single affine open of `C ×_k Spec R` (Stacks `0B8B`).  Mathlib has no form of
23	`0B8B`, and this project constructs no curve other than `P¹`, so formalising it is out of
24	scope for this lane.  It therefore appears here as the named, explicit hypothesis
25	`SwallowedBy` — a *statement to be supplied by the seed*, exactly as
26	`informal/spec-dd-r.md` ADDENDUM 3 C4(ii) requires: the geometric input is relocated into a
27	visible obligation rather than hidden inside a `LocalEquations` or an adaptation field.
28	
29	`SwallowedBy` is deliberately NOT bundled into `AffCoverData` or `AffAdaptation`.  A reader
30	can see, from any theorem's signature, whether it assumes confinement.
31	
32	## What the shape buys
33	
34	For a cover with a straddling piece, swallow-or-miss holds by construction rather than by a
35	connectivity argument, so — with no fibre, no tube, and no packet idempotent —
36	`hnoLeak` holds at every piece, clause (c1)-finite holds at every piece, and every
37	non-swallowing piece contributes a vanishing colength (`cert-collapse`).  Crucially there is
38	no dichotomy step, hence no appeal to `V₀ ⊔ V₁ = ⊤`, hence no chart.

42	* `AlgebraicGeometry.AffCoverData.SwallowedBy` — the straddling-piece hypothesis.
43	* `AffAdaptation.forall_subset_or_disjoint_of_swallowedBy` — swallow-or-miss from it.
44	* `AffAdaptation.forall_noLeak_of_swallowedBy` — the assembler's `hnoLeak`.
45	* `AffAdaptation.forall_finite_colength_of_swallowedBy` — clause (c1)-finite everywhere.
46	* `AffCoverData.ofSwallowingPiece` — the two-piece widened cover from a straddling affine

9	/-!
10	# cert-assemble on the widened cover: from a straddling piece to `DivFamZarAff`
11	
12	Roadmap leaf `AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-d.ddr.certificate.cert-assemble`, over the widened
13	predicate.  This composes the lane into one statement: **pointwise on the base, a straddling
14	affine piece plus the (c1)/(c2) inputs give a widened locally-certified system**, hence a
15	`DivFamZarAff` class.
16	
17	## What each hypothesis is, and why it is where it is
18	
19	The assembler takes, at each prime `p` of the base, an away localization `r ∉ p` over which:
20	
21	* the pulled system has an adaptation whose cover has a **straddling piece**
22	  (`SwallowedBy`) — the Stacks `0B8B` geometric input, explicit per I-0492 clause 2;
23	* the **glued clauses** (c2)/(c3)/(c4) hold.  These are NOT free: `cert-collapse` showed the
24	  diagonal of the difference arrow vanishes identically, so (c4) always forces flatness of
25	  the diagonal overlap colengths (I-0340).  They are therefore hypotheses here rather than
26	  conclusions, and that is the corrected reading of the leaf;
27	* the **fibrewise-regularity** input for (c1)-projectivity, which is I-0492 clause 4(i) in
28	  its per-piece form.  It is a hypothesis, not carrier data.
29	
30	The clauses (c1) themselves are *produced*, not assumed: `finite_colength` from the
31	straddling piece via the support-trace engine, `projective_colength` from the fibrewise
32	input via the widened flatness route.  That is the whole value the lane adds — clause (c1),
33	the one the fixed-pair design could not supply for a straddling divisor, now comes for free
34	from an affine-open cover.
35	
36	## Main declarations
37	
38	* `AffAdaptation.isCertified_of_swallowedBy` — the certificate from a straddling piece plus
39	  the glued clauses and the fibrewise input.
40	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallyCertifiedAff_of_forall_prime_swallowed` — the pointwise
41	  assembler.
42	* `AlgebraicGeometry.divFamZarAff_of_forall_prime_swallowed` — the resulting class, the
43	  object every DD-R consumer wants.
44	-/
45	
46	set_option autoImplicit false
47	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
48	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

52	open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace Opposite
53	open scoped TensorProduct
54	
55	namespace AlgebraicGeometry

57	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
58	
59	namespace AffAdaptation
60	
61	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
62	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
63	variable {D : AffCoverData C R} {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
64	variable (A : AffAdaptation D d)
65	
66	/-- **The certificate from a straddling piece.**  Clauses (c1) are PRODUCED: finiteness from
67	the straddling piece through the support-trace engine, projectivity from the fibrewise
68	regularity input through the widened flatness route (`AffCoverData.flat_sections_pieces`).
69	Clauses (c2)/(c3)/(c4) are hypotheses — by `cert-collapse`/I-0340 they cannot be free, since
70	the vanishing diagonal of the difference arrow makes (c4) imply flatness of the diagonal
71	overlap colengths for every adaptation whatsoever. -/
72	theorem isCertified_of_swallowedBy [IsProper C.hom] [IsNoetherianRing R] {n : ℕ}
73	    (hswallow : D.SwallowedBy d)
74	    (hfib : ∀ (j : D.index) (p : PrimeSpectrum R),
75	      (A.eqn j ⊗ₜ[R] (1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :
76	          Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j) ⊗[R] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ∈
77	        nonZeroDivisors
78	          (Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j) ⊗[R] p.asIdeal.ResidueField))
79	    (hfinite_glued : Module.Finite R A.Glued)
80	    (hproj_glued : Module.Projective R A.Glued)
81	    (hrank : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R, Module.rankAtStalk A.Glued p = n)
82	    (hflat_incl : Module.Flat R (A.chartProd ⧸ A.gluedSubmodule))
83	    (hflat_diff :
84	      Module.Flat R (A.ovlProd ⧸ LinearMap.range (A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight))) :
85	    A.IsCertified n := by
86	  haveI hfin : ∀ j, Module.Finite R (A.colength j) :=
87	    A.forall_finite_colength_of_swallowedBy hswallow
88	  exact
89	    { finite_colength := hfin
90	      projective_colength := fun j => by
91	        haveI := hfin j
92	        exact A.projective_colength_of_forall_tmul_residueField j (hfib j)
93	      finite_glued := hfinite_glued
94	      projective_glued := hproj_glued
95	      rankAtStalk_glued := hrank
96	      flat_coker_incl := hflat_incl
97	      flat_coker_diff := hflat_diff }
98	
99	end AffAdaptation
100	
101	/-! ## The pointwise assembler -/
102	
103	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
104	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
105	variable {n : ℕ}
106	
107	/-- **The pointwise assembler over the widened predicate.**  At every prime of the base it
108	suffices to produce an away localization carrying a widened certified family divisor-equal to
109	the pulled system; quasi-compactness of `Spec R` does the rest
110	(`isLocallyCertifiedAff_of_forall_prime_exists_away`).
111	
112	This is the widened counterpart of
113	`isLocallyCertified_of_forall_prime_exists_certified_adaptation`
114	(`DivSchemeCertZarPointwise.lean:162`): same base-side shape, but the certificate on the
115	curve side is now carried by an arbitrary affine-open cover, so a divisor straddling both
116	pinned vertical fibres is no longer excluded. -/
117	theorem isLocallyCertifiedAff_of_forall_prime_certified_adaptation
118	    {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
119	    (h : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R, ∃ r, r ∉ p.asIdeal ∧
120	      haveI : IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r)) :=
121	        isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C R (Localization.Away r) r
122	      ∃ (Dr : AffCoverData C (Localization.Away r))
123	        (A : AffAdaptation Dr
124	          (d.pullback (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r))
125	            (Scheme.LocalEquations.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_isOpenImmersion
126	              (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r)) d))),
127	        A.IsCertified n) :
128	    IsLocallyCertifiedAff n d := by
129	  refine isLocallyCertifiedAff_of_forall_prime_exists_away fun p => ?_
130	  obtain ⟨r, hrp, Dr, A, hA⟩ := h p
131	  haveI : IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r)) :=
132	    isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C R (Localization.Away r) r
133	  -- bundle the supplied cover, adaptation and certificate; the divisor equality is `rfl`
134	  exact ⟨r, hrp, ⟨_, Dr, A, hA⟩, Scheme.LocalEquations.divEq_refl _⟩
135	
136	/-- **The `DivFamZarAff` class of a system certified pointwise on the base.**  The endpoint
137	of the widened certificate lane: this is what a DD-R consumer receives, and no hypothesis on
138	`|P¹(k)|` appears anywhere in its production. -/
139	noncomputable def divFamZarAff_of_forall_prime_certified_adaptation
140	    {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
141	    (h : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R, ∃ r, r ∉ p.asIdeal ∧
142	      haveI : IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r)) :=
143	        isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C R (Localization.Away r) r
144	      ∃ (Dr : AffCoverData C (Localization.Away r))
145	        (A : AffAdaptation Dr
146	          (d.pullback (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r))
147	            (Scheme.LocalEquations.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_isOpenImmersion
148	              (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r)) d))),
149	        A.IsCertified n) :
150	    DivFamZarAff C R n :=
151	  DivFamZarAff.mk d (isLocallyCertifiedAff_of_forall_prime_certified_adaptation h)
152	
153	end AlgebraicGeometry

/-- Coefficient-iso transport of degree-one vanishing: if `H¹'(U, G)` vanishes and
`F ≅ G` globally, then `H¹'(U, F)` vanishes. -/
theorem HModule'.subsingleton_of_congrCoeff (α : F ≅ G) {n : ℕ}
    [Subsingleton (HModule' G U n)] : Subsingleton (HModule' F U n) :=
  (HModule'.congrCoeff α n).toEquiv.subsingleton

end CategoryTheory.Sheaf

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Over.sectionsAlgebra

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
variable (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]

/-- The **relative curve** `C ⊗ Spec R` over the affine test ring `R`: the underlying
scheme of the cartesian-monoidal product of `C` and `overSpec k R` in `Over (Spec k)`. -/
noncomputable def relCurve : Scheme.{u} := (C ⊗ overSpec k R).left

lemma relCurve_def : relCurve C R = (C ⊗ overSpec k R).left := rfl

/-- The relative curve is a scheme over `Spec R` via the second projection. -/
noncomputable instance relCurve.instOver : (relCurve C R).Over (Spec (.of R)) :=
  .ofHom (snd C (overSpec k R)).left

variable (D : C.left.AffineTwoCover)

/-- The **base-changed affine two-cover** of the relative curve: the preimages of the
charts of `D` under the first projection `relCurve C R ⟶ C.left`
(`Scheme.AffineTwoCover.pullbackProd`), an affine two-chart cover of `relCurve C R`. -/
noncomputable def relCover : (relCurve C R).AffineTwoCover := D.pullbackProd R

/-- The first base-changed chart is affine (`G-CBC-1`). -/
theorem relCover_isAffineOpen₀ : IsAffineOpen (relCover C R D).V₀ :=
  (relCover C R D).isAffineOpen₀

/-- The second base-changed chart is affine (`G-CBC-1`). -/
theorem relCover_isAffineOpen₁ : IsAffineOpen (relCover C R D).V₁ :=
  (relCover C R D).isAffineOpen₁

/-- The two base-changed charts cover the relative curve (`G-CBC-1`). -/
theorem relCover_sup : (relCover C R D).V₀ ⊔ (relCover C R D).V₁ = ⊤ :=
  (relCover C R D).sup_eq_top

/-- **CBC-0 (relative carrier).** For the structure sheaf of the relative curve as a sheaf
of `R`-modules, the degree-one cohomology over `Spec R` is the cokernel of the two-cover
restriction-difference map on `R`-module sections. This is
`Scheme.twoCoverH1LinearEquiv`/`TwoCover.h1CokEquiv` instantiated at `k := R`,
`X := relCurve C R`, `F := 𝒪`, with the two affine-vanishing instances discharged by the
landed structure-sheaf vanishing. -/
noncomputable def relTwoCoverH1 :
    Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C R).moduleKSheaf R) 1 ≃ₗ[R]
      TwoCover.H1Cok R (relCurve C R) (relCover C R D).V₀ (relCover C R D).V₁ :=
  TwoCover.h1CokEquiv R (relCurve C R) (relCover C R D).V₀ (relCover C R D).V₁
    (relCover_sup C R D) (relCover_isAffineOpen₀ C R D) (relCover_isAffineOpen₁ C R D)

/-- The overlap of the two base-changed charts is the preimage of the overlap of `D`. -/
theorem relCover_inf :
    (relCover C R D).V₀ ⊓ (relCover C R D).V₁ =
      (fst C (overSpec k R)).left ⁻¹ᵁ (D.V₀ ⊓ D.V₁) :=
  (Scheme.Hom.preimage_inf (fst C (overSpec k R)).left).symm

section StandingBundle

variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]

/-- **H⁰ base change / CBC-3 anchor.** For the challenge curve `C`, the degree-zero
cohomology of the structure sheaf on the relative curve is the test ring itself:
`Γ(C_R, ⊤) ≃+* R`, universally in the commutative `k`-algebra `R`. This is Kleiman's
`𝒪_S ≅ f_* 𝒪_X` (`Over.universalSections`) read as an on-the-nose base-change statement:
`H⁰(C_R, 𝒪) = R = R ⊗_k k = H⁰(C, 𝒪) ⊗_k R`, the degree-zero case of "cohomology commutes
with base change". -/
noncomputable def relStructureSectionsTop : Γ(relCurve C R, ⊤) ≃+* R :=
  (Over.universalSectionsEquiv C R).symm

end StandingBundle

end AlgebraicGeometry

/-- Restriction of sections of the relative curve as an `R`-algebra homomorphism
(`Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra` structures on both sides). -/
noncomputable def relResAlgHom {W V : (relCurve C R).Opens} (h : W ≤ V) :
    Γ(relCurve C R, V) →ₐ[R] Γ(relCurve C R, W) :=
  AlgHom.mk' (CommRingCat.Hom.hom ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE h).op))
    (fun c x => by
      simp only [Algebra.smul_def]
      rw [map_mul]
      congr 1
      rw [Scheme.algebraMap_overSectionsAlgebra, Scheme.algebraMap_overSectionsAlgebra]
      exact (relCurve C R).overAlgebraMap_apply_res R (homOfLE h).op c)

@[simp]
lemma relResAlgHom_apply {W V : (relCurve C R).Opens} (h : W ≤ V) (s : Γ(relCurve C R, V)) :
    relResAlgHom C R h s = ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE h).op).hom s :=
  rfl

/-- **The finite chart adaptation of a local-equation system** (worksheet §1.1 (D1)):
basic-open cover data of the two pinned charts, equations `f_j` on the pieces, and the
pointwise refinement clause `eqn_rel` — on the overlap of each piece with any member of
`d.cover`, `f_j` agrees with `d`'s equation up to a unit. Regularity of the `f_j` is
DERIVED (`DivisorAdaptation.eqn_regular`), not stored. -/
structure DivisorAdaptation [IsAffineHom π] (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations) :
    Type u extends FinCoverData C R π where
  /-- The equation on the piece `D(h_j)`. -/
  eqn : ∀ j : toFinCoverData.index, Γ(relCurve C R, toFinCoverData.pieces j)
  /-- The equations refine `d` pointwise up to units: on the overlap of each piece with
  any member of `d`'s cover, `f_j` and `d`'s equation differ by a unit. Point-free (the
  `DivEq` spelling), so it pulls back along arbitrary morphisms — the resolution of the
  DD-1 pt-transport seam (`informal/spec-dd-2.md` §1a). The quantifier ranges over ALL
  `y`: the empty overlap carries the zero ring, where the clause is trivial. -/

/-! ### The colength modules and the glued equalizer -/

/-- The chart-local colength module `Γ(D(h_j)) ⧸ (f_j)`, an `R`-algebra through
`Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra`. -/
noncomputable abbrev colength (j : A.index) : Type u :=
  Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces j) ⧸ Ideal.span {A.eqn j}

/-- The symmetric overlap ideal: both equations restricted to the piece overlap. The
two restrictions generate the same ideal (the equations differ by units on overlaps
through the refinement witness), but the symmetric span needs no transport in the
DEFINITION. -/
noncomputable abbrev ovlIdeal (i j : A.index) :
    Ideal Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j) :=
  Ideal.span
    {relResAlgHom C R (inf_le_left : A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j ≤ A.pieces i) (A.eqn i),
     relResAlgHom C R (inf_le_right : A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j ≤ A.pieces j) (A.eqn j)}

/-- The overlap colength module `Γ(D(h_i) ⊓ D(h_j)) ⧸ (f_i, f_j)`. -/
noncomputable abbrev ovlColength (i j : A.index) : Type u :=
  Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j) ⧸ A.ovlIdeal i j

/-- The induced `R`-algebra map `colength i → ovlColength i j` (restrict, then quotient;
the ideal of `f_i` lands in the symmetric span). -/
noncomputable def toOvlLeft (i j : A.index) : A.colength i →ₐ[R] A.ovlColength i j :=
  Ideal.Quotient.liftₐ (Ideal.span {A.eqn i})
    ((Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ R (A.ovlIdeal i j)).comp (relResAlgHom C R inf_le_left))
    (by
      intro a ha
      rw [Ideal.mem_span_singleton] at ha
      obtain ⟨c, rfl⟩ := ha
      simp only [AlgHom.comp_apply, map_mul]
      have hmem : relResAlgHom C R
          (inf_le_left : A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j ≤ A.pieces i) (A.eqn i)
          ∈ A.ovlIdeal i j :=
        Ideal.subset_span (Set.mem_insert _ _)
      rw [Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ_eq_mk, Ideal.Quotient.eq_zero_iff_mem.mpr hmem, zero_mul])

/-- The induced `R`-algebra map `colength j → ovlColength i j`. -/
noncomputable def toOvlRight (i j : A.index) : A.colength j →ₐ[R] A.ovlColength i j :=
  Ideal.Quotient.liftₐ (Ideal.span {A.eqn j})
    ((Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ R (A.ovlIdeal i j)).comp (relResAlgHom C R inf_le_right))
    (by
      intro a ha
      rw [Ideal.mem_span_singleton] at ha
      obtain ⟨c, rfl⟩ := ha
      simp only [AlgHom.comp_apply, map_mul]
      have hmem : relResAlgHom C R
          (inf_le_right : A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j ≤ A.pieces j) (A.eqn j)
          ∈ A.ovlIdeal i j :=
        Ideal.subset_span (Set.mem_insert_of_mem _ rfl)
      rw [Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ_eq_mk, Ideal.Quotient.eq_zero_iff_mem.mpr hmem, zero_mul])

/-- The product of the chart-local colength modules (an `abbrev`, so the `Pi.module`
instances apply directly — probe finding, spec §1b(iii)). -/
noncomputable abbrev chartProd : Type u := ∀ j : A.index, A.colength j

/-- The product of the overlap colength modules over ordered index pairs. -/
noncomputable abbrev ovlProd : Type u := ∀ p : A.index × A.index, A.ovlColength p.1 p.2

/-- The left arrow of the equalizer: restrict the `p.1` component to each overlap. -/
noncomputable def deltaLeft : A.chartProd →ₗ[R] A.ovlProd :=
  LinearMap.pi
    (fun p : A.index × A.index => (A.toOvlLeft p.1 p.2).toLinearMap ∘ₗ LinearMap.proj p.1)

/-- The right arrow of the equalizer: restrict the `p.2` component to each overlap. -/
noncomputable def deltaRight : A.chartProd →ₗ[R] A.ovlProd :=
  LinearMap.pi
    (fun p : A.index × A.index => (A.toOvlRight p.1 p.2).toLinearMap ∘ₗ LinearMap.proj p.2)
